title: Towards a Just and Humane Society in the DiGi Age
keywords: do the least you can do
primary_topics: Closing address at the FLP 2020 Awards Ceremony (online, Independence Day June 12, 2020) -- first pandemic-era ceremony
The DiGi Age thesis: lawyers with a heart and conscience are irreplaceable by AI robots because only humans can dispense compassionate justice when the law is unclear, inadequate, or unconscionable
The 'little things' philosophy: the Lucila Takjerad Harvard story and CJP's own bar-review benefactor -- small gestures of kindness that twist and turn destinies
Commissioning the FLP scholars as the future leaders of the DiGi generation -- the 10-to-20-year horizon
sub_topics: Thanks to CJ Diosdado M. Peralta and SAJ Estela M. Perlas-Bernabe (Board of Judges for Scholarship and Dissertation Contest respectively); Tan Yan Kee Foundation (Scholarship Program); Ayala Group (Dissertation Writing Contest)
Bar topnotchers and passers honored; 100% passing rate tradition; new batches of scholars and dissertation winners

Lucila Takjerad's Harvard story: Algerian refugee, 1994 civil war; illiterate mother couldn't write her name on the French emigration list; a stranger ran after her, scribbled her name; the family emigrated to France; Lucila became first woman in her family to graduate Harvard; her message: 'do the most you can do... but also do the least you can do. Because the least you can do might turn out to be the most significant'

CJP's own poor beginning: peddled newspapers, shined shoes in grade and high school; sold bibles to professors and textbooks to classmates; both parents died while he was in pre-law and law; stranded with no money for bar review; an older friend offered to pay for bar review (books + modest monthly stipend) on one condition -- land among the Top Ten; CJP was hospitalized during the first Sunday of the bar exams; law dean Salonga urged him not to quit; landed sixth place ('Alleluia!')

The friend's unknowing gift: 'My friend, who is now deceased, never knew how his simple gesture of paying for my pre-bar expenses brought me over to the noble legal profession and, eventually, to the highest judicial position in our country'

FLP's 'little things': financial grants, SC interviews, board of judges questioning, midnight dissertation-writing, secretariat kindness -- 'valuable little things that may twist and turn your careers'
Urging scholars to join and move the FLPSS: give bits of knowledge and wisdom to future applicants; the Society as networking podium, giving-back vehicle, and DiGi Age riding platform
AI challenge to lawyers: robots will become instant legal encyclopedias applying facts times law equals decision (FxL=D); dura lex, sed lex automated

CJP's response: 'only humans have a heart, only humans have wisdom, only humans can dispense compassionate justice especially when the law is not clear, when the law is inadequate, or when the law is unconscionable'

Future-leaders commissioning: 'In 10 or 20 years, you will be the leaders of the DiGi generation... the super lawyers, the justices and judges, the legislators and cabinet members, even the chief justices and presidents'
Hovering-spirit close: 'my spirit will be hovering above you, beside you and behind you, smiling and contented, that I have brought you a few little things'

stances.claim: Good lawyers bred by liberty and prosperity under the rule of law will not be made obsolete by AI robots in the DiGi Age because only humans can dispense compassionate justice when the law is unclear, inadequate, or unconscionable. The automated FxL=D formula applies dura lex, sed lex perfectly -- but justice requires a human heart and conscience beyond the formula.
stances.rhetorical_move: human-irreplaceability argument: the three conditions where the law fails (unclear, inadequate, unconscionable) as the permanent space for human judicial judgment that AI cannot occupy

stances.claim: Small, simple, often unnoticed acts of kindness -- a stranger writing a mother's name on a list; an older friend paying bar review expenses -- are the most significant life-changing forces. The 'little things' philosophy inverts the Harvard injunction ('do the most you can do') by adding: 'also do the least you can do, because the least you can do might turn out to be the most significant.'
stances.rhetorical_move: least-is-most inversion: reframes impact calculus to make small gestures morally urgent

CJP was hospitalized during the first Sunday of the bar exams; Salonga urged him not to quit. He landed sixth place. The friend -- now deceased -- 'never knew how his simple gesture of paying for my pre-bar expenses brought me over to the noble legal profession and, eventually, to the highest judicial position in our country.'

The AI legal-formula challenge: 'Many say that the DiGi Age may eliminate lawyers because robots will become instant encyclopedias of law with instant ways of applying them... the automatic application of the Austinian formula of facts times law equals decision or FxL=D.' CJP's counter: 'only humans have a heart... only lawyers with a heart, with a conscience can dispense compassionate justice in a just and humane society.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered June 12, 2020 -- Independence Day -- as the closing address at FLP's first pandemic-era online awards ceremony, this speech by CJP opens with thanks to CJ Diosdado Peralta and SAJ Estela Perlas-Bernabe (Board of Judges chairs) and the Tan Yan Kee Foundation and Ayala Group, and acknowledges that bar exams have been postponed by COVID. The governing philosophy is the 'little things' thesis, illustrated by two stories. The first is Lucila Takjerad's Harvard commencement: a 1994 Algerian civil war refugee's illiterate mother couldn't write her name on the French emigration list; a stranger scribbled it; the family emigrated to France; Lucila graduated Harvard and proposed: 'Fellow graduates, of course, do the most you can do... But also do the least you can do. Because, the least you can do might turn out to be the most significant.' The second is CJP's own story: both parents dead, no money for bar review, an anonymous older friend paid for it on condition he land in the Top Ten; CJP was hospitalized during the first bar Sunday but Salonga urged him not to quit; he landed sixth place. The friend 'never knew how his simple gesture... brought me over to the noble legal profession and, eventually, to the highest judicial position in our country.' CJP positions FLP's own programs -- grants, SC interviews, board questioning, midnight dissertation-writing, secretariat kindness -- as the institutionalized version of that stranger's gesture. He then addresses the AI challenge: DiGi Age robots may apply FxL=D (facts times law equals decision) and dura lex, sed lex automatically -- but 'only humans have a heart, only humans have wisdom, only humans can dispense compassionate justice especially when the law is not clear, when the law is inadequate, or when the law is unconscionable.' He commissions the scholars as 'the leaders of the DiGi generation' in 10-20 years, closing with the hovering-spirit promise: 'my spirit will be hovering above you, beside you and behind you, smiling and contented, that I have brought you a few little things that have made a vital difference.'
